image_prompt.text: One continuous walking path representing an accumulated life, running through kitchens, campsites, apartments, hospital rooms and family homes rather than around them
A transition element at every age boundary - a wall, hallway or doorway - that blocks the view behind while the earlier path is extended
The far side of each transition opens out so that turning around reveals the whole accumulated path stretching back behind the player
Early memories sit close and readable beside the path; the oldest ones read as distant lights and landmark silhouettes far behind
Enterable memory interiors along the path - childhood kitchen, packed bedroom, first shared apartment, family home, hospital room
Family and friends acting out each memory in place - cutting fruit, laughing, interrupting each other, a child taking first steps - continuing as the player passes
Each finished chapter drops away behind the transition so the player cannot walk back into it, only look at it

A physical week chart standing at every transition: 90 rows of 52 squares, 4,680 in total, lived weeks filled in, the current week glowing, aging from a colourful childhood poster into a faded framed object

Recurring props re-sited chapter by chapter: a teddy bear that is comforted, packed away, rediscovered, handed on and repaired, and one family photograph on a childhood wall, in a moving box, in a hospital room and in a final gathering

layout_placement.text: Ground occupied by each memory's cast, three to five active scenes per chapter
Narrative object placements at each memory - the teddy bear and the original family photograph - marked so they can be re-dressed as the chapter changes
An observation stop at each transition where the player pauses, reads the chart and turns around before continuing
The terminal memory: the childhood kitchen the path returns to after the hospital sequence, entered as a static observer and closing the run

mechanics: Target runtime 12-18 minutes
Elevated third-person camera for most of the game, switching to first person for the final hospital scene
Player can walk, turn around, pause and observe, and perform occasional simple interactions
No combat, failure state, branching narrative or dialogue choice
Day percentage shown as 100 / days lived, e.g. WEEK 365 / TODAY IS 0.0391% OF YOUR LIFE SO FAR
Age state, path state, teddy bear state, photo state and music state tracked per modular chapter
Original score: folk-pop progression, a childhood piano melody that returns transformed, a cathartic finale that builds with every blink
Audio cues from behind the player at each transition - parent laughing, camera shutter, campfire, child's footsteps, teddy bear music, someone calling their name
Final sequence: faces morph through people from the player's life, blink transitions between static memory tableaux, camera flash to white
Credits roll over black then reveal the whole path from far above with one week square still lit
notes: Preset Story kept, but its shape world-chaptered (P4) was replaced with route-guided (P0): the prompt's central mechanic is that the earlier path stays visible behind the player, which separate maps cannot express. Chapters are zones of one continuous surface - genre note 'linear does not automatically mean multi-zone' applies exactly.
P3 comes from two picks that are genuinely indoors: the memory interiors the path passes through, and reveal-exit's threshold.

The run's terminus was inferred from the prompt's final memory rather than asked: winner-zone taken from Obby & Platformer's table via options.md, worded as the closing childhood kitchen. It carries no reward - if downstream reads WinnerZone as a prize room this is the wrong container.

Framing tension recorded rather than resolved: the credits ask for the entire life path readable from far above, while the memory scenes need furniture-level detail. Both cannot occupy one isometric render; the aerial reveal is likely a separate framing pass.

notes_for_us: Adventure has no option for a readable data surface - a chart, board, scoreboard or diagram that is the point of the space rather than decoration. tracker-quest is the nearest and it is a quest board; the week chart is the game's thesis object and it shipped as free text.

The turn-around reveal is reveal-exit run backwards. The catalogue words it as an exit opening onto something ahead, and its P3 is about a cave mouth; using it for a look-back reveal drags a P3 that may not be earned.

gate-oneway and the prompt's core instruction are in tension in a way the skill has no way to record: the prompt wants the old path permanently visible but never says whether it is walkable. One-way geometry that blocks the view would break the game; one that only blocks walking is fine. Same option ID, opposite outcomes.

Six named segments and only one may carry the top-level shape, so five chapters emitted with shape null even though they are all the same corridor. The rule reads as if a null shape means 'undescribed', but here it means 'identical to the parent'.

P2 is earned twice over and not from the biome split: sky lanes above the streets, accessible slums under them, and floating islands with cloud platforms between them all overhang. Extent and detail cannot both be honoured here and the prompt forbids the usual fix. notes_for_us: The route-override table lists world-open-biomes and the prompt said 'seamless', so this was mechanical - but the override only removes P4. It says nothing about what happens to the detail budget, and the reason P4 existed for this shape was that four biomes in one frame lose their detail. Overriding the route does not make the frame bigger, so the override quietly converts a pipeline cost into a quality loss with no field to record it in.

Four boss arenas are four distinct combat spaces and hazard-aggro was the only row that would hold them. A named boss arena with its own geometry is not an aggro bowl; it is closer to Action's space-bounded, but one shape is already spent on the world.

The dragon fight is fought in the air, boarding a flying boss. Nothing in the loaded genres or the catalogue expresses a combat volume with no floor - volume-open-air is a Racing/Adventure shape and the shape slot was gone.

Segment shape for four of five zones came out null because only one shape is allowed above and the zones are not separately shaped. Same problem as the chaptered prompt in this batch: null is being used to mean both 'undescribed' and 'inherits the parent'.
